qc.label_under_test: A year of the 1880s or 1890s written in digits, in any language and script, including native digit systems such as Arabic-Indic, Persian or Devanagari digits (those fire about half to three-quarters as strongly) (peaks on the decade digit: 18|8|x, 18|9|x, and '1890s'); years 1900-1909 fire about half as strongly, fading toward the end of that decade (1907-1909 about 0.1-0.2); years of the 1870s are in between (about 0.13-0.47, on the 7: often above 0.3, so they are neither clean fires nor clean misses); years before 1870 (including the 1850s-1860s, this neuron's other pole), the 1910s-1990s, 2000-2079 and earlier centuries stay quiet (under about 0.1), in native digits too; future years 2080-2099 used as years fire weakly (about 0.2-0.35); 1880s-1890s years spelled out in words fire weakly (about 0.1-0.3) and short forms like '89 stay quiet; late-19th-century era words with no 188x/189x digits (Gilded Age, fin de siecle) stay quiet. A bare four-digit 188x/189x code or ID in a modern setting (a PIN, password, gate or discount code, serial or phone-number ending) is in between (about 0.1-0.3), neither a clean fire nor a clean miss; a 188x/189x product or model number standing next to a brand or the word 'model' in a modern setting is also in between but can be strong (about 0.1-0.65), so it is neither a clean fire nor a clean miss; a 188x/189x count, distance, price, route or room number is weak in a modern or neutral setting (about 0.02-0.2) but fires (about 0.2-0.6) when the text is set in the late 19th century, either through an earlier 1880s-1890s year or through a period cue such as the Gilded Age, the Wild West or Victorian England; after an earlier 1850s-1870s year it is unreliable (sometimes strong, up to about 0.8); written with a thousands comma (1,89x) it reaches about 0.15-0.4 in any setting

neighbours.label: A year of the 1880s or 1890s written in digits, peaking on the decade digit (18|8|x, 18|9|x, '1890s'), in any language's text. Native digits split: Arabic-Indic, Persian, Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Kannada, Myanmar and full-width digits fire about half to three-quarters as strongly, as do years written digit by digit in Chinese numerals; Thai, Lao, Telugu and Tibetan digits stay quiet (under 0.1) even in English, and Tamil, Malayalam and Khmer digits are in between (0.05-0.35). 1900-1909 fire about half as strongly, fading to 0.1-0.2 by 1907-1909; the 1870s are in between (0.13-0.47); years before 1870, 1910-2079 and earlier centuries stay quiet, in any digits; 2080-2099 fire weakly (0.2-0.35); 1880s-90s years in words fire weakly (0.1-0.3), '89 stays quiet, era words with no such digits stay quiet. A 188x/189x code, PIN or ID in a modern setting is in between (0.1-0.3); a 188x/189x model number beside a brand or 'model' is in between but can reach 0.65; a 188x/189x count, distance, price or room number is weak (0.02-0.2) unless the text is set in the late 19th century (then 0.2-0.6), unreliable after an earlier 1850s-1870s year (up to 0.8), and 0.15-0.4 with a thousands comma (1,89x).
